hints: Focus on what the final oxidation product must contain to pass both tests at once.
Recall that 2,4-DNPH needs a carbonyl group, while alkaline iodine needs specifically a methyl ketone group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$.
Oxidise each alcohol in your head to a ketone and check if that ketone keeps a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ unit.
walkthrough:
**Decode the two tests**

Think about what functional group the product must have. A positive 2,4-DNPH means an aldehyde or ketone is present, giving an orange precipitate.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone + 2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**Add the iodoform condition**

A positive alkaline aqueous iodine test means a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$. This needs a methyl ketone group.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-R + \text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 \text{(yellow s)}$$

**Test alcohol 1 and alcohol 3**

Alcohol 1 is cyclohexanol, a secondary alcohol. Oxidation gives cyclohexanone. This is a ketone so DNPH positive, but it has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group so iodoform negative. So 1 fails.

Alcohol 3 is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$, a secondary alcohol of type $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})-$. Oxidation gives $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{COCH}_3$, a methyl ketone. This gives both precipitates. So 3 succeeds.

**Test the tricky molecule 2**

Molecule 2 already contains a methyl ketone, $\text{COCH}_3$, plus a secondary alcohol on the ring. Gentle oxidation converts the $\text{CH}-\text{OH}$ to $\text{C}=\text{O}$, but leaves the $\text{COCH}_3$ untouched.

The product is a diketone containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so it is DNPH positive and iodoform positive. So 2 succeeds. Therefore only 2 and 3 work.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests 1, 2 and 3 all work. Alcohol 1 oxidises only to cyclohexanone, which lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group and so cannot give the yellow iodoform precipitate.
options.B: Incorrect. This suggests 1 and 2 only. It wrongly includes 1, whose product cyclohexanone is iodoform negative, and wrongly excludes 3, whose product is a classic methyl ketone.
options.C: Correct. Alcohol 3 oxidises to $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{COCH}_3$, a methyl ketone. Alcohol 2 oxidises to a diketone that still contains its original $\text{COCH}_3$ group. Both products are ketones for DNPH and methyl ketones for iodoform.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only 3 works. It correctly identifies 3 but misses 2. Students often forget that in 2 the existing methyl ketone survives oxidation of the separate alcohol group.
